newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf getting back to normal after French strike.
newsitem.headline: Elf getting back to normal after French strike.

text.p: Elf Aquitaine said on Monday its three French oil refineries were moving progressively back to normal after a nine-day strike which ended on Friday.
"All the refineries are on their way. The main issue for us is safety, making sure everythig is started up in a normal manner," an Elf spokesman said.
Workers at the 128,000 barrels per day (bpd) Feyzin plant near Lyon, who held out for strike pay when the protest ended at other plants, returned to work on Saturday morning, he said.
Production at the 215,000 bpd Donges plant has been nearly normal since Sunday, he added.
The 98,000 bpd Grandpuits refinery near Paris would be back to normal very soon.
"The situation at each refinery is becoming progressively normal," the spokesman said. "Deliveries have been going all right since Saturday."
Workers at refining and distribution subsidiary Elf Antar called off their strike after nine days on Friday.
Strikers voted at Grandpuits to accept an Elf pay offer, triggering the strike's breakdown at the two other plants.
The strike was initially called over plans to phase out 330 jobs in Elf's downstream division in France.
